My question is simply this: You've told the Trial Chamber that you know that he was appointed to operate the -- as a commander. Do you have any information as to who appointed him to that position?

utterances.speaker: PJETER SHALA
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber how you know that he was appointed if you don't know who appointed him?

utterances.speaker: PJETER SHALA
utterances.text: When we went to Gllogjan to assist them when it was attacked, most of the group we were in remained to work with some young lads there. I don't know who appointed him. And it was none of my business to find out.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you ever know? Did you ever have any knowledge as to who it was that created or appointed him as -- who appointed him as leader or commander of this special unit?

utterances.speaker: PJETER SHALA
utterances.text: According to rumours, I might make suppositions, but I wasn't present in the meeting that appointed him or who the person who appointed him was. There are, however, many rumours to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Well, what information did you have as to who appointed him commander of the special --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry. Before the witness answers that question, he's already indicated that the source of his supposition is rumours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Mr. -- Mr. Emmerson, the question Mr. Di Fazio puts to the witness, that what information he heard, is the first question to explore further what the basis of that information was. And the qualification as hearsay information, as rumours is not uncommon; so therefore, Mr. Di Fazio may proceed. Please proceed, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What information did you have as to who -- who appointed him commander of the special unit?

utterances.speaker: PJETER SHALA
utterances.text: According to my personal opinion and according to what I heard from other soldiers, I think it was Ramush who appointed him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. Di Fazio, we'll try to find out a bit more detail. You first said you were not present at the meeting where he was appointed, so that suggests that he was appointed in a meeting.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I suppose so. This must have been so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, some -- sometimes people can be appointed outside of a meeting. When did you learn about a meeting, if at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't have any precise information, because it was not part of my duty to find out what meetings were held, where these meetings were held. But I heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Shala, from --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You said, "I didn't have any precise information." Tell us what information you had.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thought that for anyone to be appointed to a certain post should be appointed by Ramush. That was my personal opinion and maybe also the opinion of many others in the local population there, because Ramush was the commander of that zone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now I asked you what information did you have. When did you become aware of Togeri being appointed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After I went to Dujake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, who told you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard from the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you remember which soldier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I very much regret it, but there were many soldiers coming and going. They happened to pass through that area. So I can't be precise from whom I'd heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What did the soldier tell you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That a very good unit is established and that Togeri is its commander, a very capable unit. Someone called it Suta. All sorts of names they were giving to it. Actually, it was a special unit. And these are all based on hearsay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How do you know? How do you know that the -- how do you know that the soldier did not attend that meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I don't know what to say. These were rumours circulating around. That was a time when such rumours circulated. Nobody could attend a meeting where I stayed in Dujake. Only at night I could move about, because during the day it was impossible for us to move about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, please proceed. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And about how big was the unit, if you can tell us, please?

utterances.speaker: PJETER SHALA
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know how big it was. On an average, a unit had 30, 40 members. But this is just a supposition. I didn't count them. Maybe it had more. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. And can you tell us what sort of uniform, if any, they wore.

utterances.speaker: PJETER SHALA
utterances.text: They wore brown uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And what uniform did you wear as a -- as a military policeman?

utterances.speaker: PJETER SHALA
utterances.text: Black uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And when you saw the individual called Togeri, did you -- what sort of uniform did he wear?

utterances.speaker: PJETER SHALA
utterances.text: We could change the uniforms at will. Sometimes we wore camouflage uniforms. Sometimes black uniforms. It was a time when we were not obliged to wear a certain type of uniform. I personally wore camouflage, black uniforms. When I washed one pair of uniform, I put on the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And -- but just let's go back to Togeri. What sort of uniform did he have on when you saw him? Or did it change?

utterances.speaker: PJETER SHALA
utterances.text: I don't remember accurately. He would normally wear brown or camouflage uniform. Many years have passed since that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And could -- was it easy to visit the location or base of these -- of this elite unit or special -- sorry, special unit?

utterances.speaker: PJETER SHALA
utterances.text: I didn't have anything to do with that unit, but to go there you had to ask for special permission, because the other units didn't meddle with that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And do you know from whom -- or can you recall from whom you had to get the special authorisation?

utterances.speaker: PJETER SHALA
utterances.text: From Ramush.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thanks. You -- you mentioned earlier in your evidence that you went to Dujak. Can the witness be shown P159. And for the witness's assistance, can we make the -- the -- the Albanian version a little bigger. Thank you. Just have a look at that document, please. What that document says is that it's created on the 2nd of July. It's signed by the commander, Ramush Haradinaj, and it ostensibly appoints you -- relocates you to Dukagjin and it's dated the 2nd of July, 1998.

utterances.speaker: PJETER SHALA
utterances.text: To Dujake, not Dukagjin.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: That's my -- my mistake. I'm sorry. To -- to Dujak. Did you -- can you tell the Trial Chamber this: It's dated the 2nd of July, but when were you -- actually in Dujak? Around that time or before or after?

utterances.speaker: PJETER SHALA
utterances.text: On the same day that I was given the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And that's your signature on the document, is it? I think it says "Ujku." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PJETER SHALA
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thanks. I've finished with that. MR. DI FAZIO: I may actually be on time. 5.15, if Your Honours please. Can the witness be shown 65 ter 2120.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It needs a number, Mr. Di Fazio? MR. DI FAZIO: It will. It will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, that would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be P1188.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: All right. Have a -- have a read of that document. Thank you. And it -- is that your signature? In fact, is that your signature that appears twice on the document?

utterances.speaker: PJETER SHALA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And it's dated the 23rd of July, 1998, and it -- it's -- it appears to you that you're asking that the Local Staff in Dujake be -- be called to report, because they're not handling issues properly. And it says that it went to the Operative Staff of the Dukagjini Zone. Why did you create that document?

utterances.speaker: PJETER SHALA
utterances.text: Because I didn't have any support there. I was -- my work was undermined all the time, and I needed support. People engaged in all sorts of propaganda and I needed to have some -- some support.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. So you were writing to the Operative Staff and trying to get them to help you with your problems. Is that -- is that right?

utterances.speaker: PJETER SHALA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I seek to tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objection? Then it is P1188, admitted into evidence. Could I add one question. Mr. Shala, in this document it reads: "The advantage is given to the less-preferred individuals." Who are less-preferred individuals?

utterances.speaker: PJETER SHALA
utterances.text: People who -- who had -- who had cooperated with the Serb police, who had -- out of schools [as interpreted]. They were more favoured than us, more preferred than us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you actually deliver that document to the Operative Staff of the Dukagjini Zone?

utterances.speaker: PJETER SHALA
utterances.text: No. I sent it through a soldier. I didn't know whether it was received by the Operational Staff, but the fact is they never received any reply from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And you -- earlier today you were talking about your various movements around the -- around the area. You said that -- and at one point you mentioned that you had gone to Glodjane. Can you just put that into perspective for the Trial Chamber. I would just like to be clear about that. We know that you crossed the mountains. We know that you eventually made your way to Jablanica. Now, at what point did you -- did you go to Glodjane?

utterances.speaker: PJETER SHALA
utterances.text: When Glodjane was attacked - I don't remember the exact date now - we went there as reinforcement to protect that area as much as we could.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. And apart from that, did you ever spend any time in Glodjane?

utterances.speaker: PJETER SHALA
utterances.text: After this attack, when the soldiers returned we stayed there for a couple of days. I don't know how many days. I didn't keep track of the days. It was not my responsibility to do so. We were sheltered by the villagers, because we were there to protect the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. But apart from this -- you're talking about the attack on the Haradinaj compound. Is -- about that period of time. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PJETER SHALA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Now, what I -- what I'm asking you, though, is -- is this: Apart from that, did you ever go to Glodjane and spend some time there? A few days or -- in carrying out your work and duties.

utterances.speaker: PJETER SHALA
utterances.text: After the staff was relocated there, when it was considered a free zone, I went there several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And put that in relation to -- to Dujake, or -- or your period of time in Dujak. Was that before or after you went to Dujak?

utterances.speaker: PJETER SHALA
utterances.text: Before I went to Dujake.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. So you went to Jablanica. And apart from going to Glodjane at the time that the Haradinaj compound was attacked, you stayed in Jablanica. Then you went to Glodjane for a period of time. And then finally to Dujak. Correct? Do I -- is that the sequence?

utterances.speaker: PJETER SHALA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: I think the witness has explained that before -- he went to Dujak before he went to Glodjane. MR. DI FAZIO: Well, we -- we've got to be clear about this as best we can.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Think back and think of the sequence. His Honour wants some clarity on this. You -- you've told us already about coming down to Jablanica. Now, was Glodjane before you went to Dujak or after or possibly both? I -- I don't know.

utterances.speaker: PJETER SHALA
utterances.text: Yeah, it was before and after. Of course. Even the last time when I left Kosova I went to Gllogjan again, because I had to go there with the new soldiers to get arms and I needed financial support and a written order. So from Dujake I went there afterwards as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I see. Okay. So you went there from time to time as business -- as -- as your work required you to.

utterances.speaker: PJETER SHALA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you -- were you ever based there for a period of time, such as, for example, you were based in Jablanica and Dujak?

utterances.speaker: PJETER SHALA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: For how long in Glodjane?

utterances.speaker: PJETER SHALA
utterances.text: Maybe one week, two weeks. I can't be precise. I just accompanied or escorted people who came and wanted to go to Gllogjan with Musa -- we called him Uncle Musa. Together we escorted these people up to Jabllanice. Sometimes we had to do it two or three times a night. MR. DI FAZIO: I've just got one document left, if Your Honours please. Can the witness be shown 65 ter 2119.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It needs a number, I take it? Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be P1189.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. MR. DI FAZIO: We have the Albanian, I -- I hope. Yes. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Mr. Shala, could I just ask you to look at this particular document. It -- I think it's safe to lead you on this. It seems you've signed this document. And that's your signature on the bottom left-hand corner. But it -- it's signed by Mr. Haradinaj and dated 29 June 1998 and says --

utterances.speaker: PJETER SHALA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: It says this -- there's an authorisation for work-related visit. Have -- are you familiar with that document? Have you ever seen it before?

utterances.speaker: PJETER SHALA
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And under what circumstances? Can you recall?

utterances.speaker: PJETER SHALA
utterances.text: It was an authorisation I received to go together with some soldiers to Albania to get arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. And did Mr. Haradinaj -- was this during one of the periods of time when you were in Glodjane, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: PJETER SHALA
utterances.text: I don't know the exact time, but I went to Gllogjan for every piece of document I needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And every time you went to collect weapons in Albania, did you get something similar to this to enable you to -- to carry out your duties?

utterances.speaker: PJETER SHALA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Not only me. Everyone had to do that. Everyone who was a member of the Dukagjin Plateau had to go there as a member of the army. If he went there on behalf of a village, it was something else. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I seek to tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections against P1189? No objections. Admitted into evidence. Mr. Di Fazio, does this conclude your ... MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much. Mr. Shala, we will have a break until 20 minutes to 6.00. After the break, you'll be cross-examined by Defence counsel. We'll adjourn until 20 minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I have no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have no questions. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: No questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Shala --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Shala, this then concludes your testimony in this court, because the Bench have no questions for you. And, Mr. Di Fazio, of course, I cut you down in time. MR. DI FAZIO: Well, thank you, Your Honours. And I know that I exceeded my time limit, and all is well that ends well. I think I essentially covered the main topics I wanted to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So there's -- so therefore it's clear there's no application under those circumstances where some time is left to use any remaining time. Mr. Shala, I would like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague, for answering all the questions that were put to you, and I wish you a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too. And I wish you all the success and justice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are there any procedural matters at this moment? I remember that yesterday the Defence asked for additional time to more thoroughly study the ten annexes of the previous witness. Have you finished that already? If not --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The answer, as far as -- on behalf of Mr. Balaj is, no, not yet. And we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not yet. No, that's understandable. I can imagine it that came -- well, I couldn't say it that comes as a surprise, because you presented the surprise.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's purely an organisational matter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- and it's a question of transferring over references, but we will have it resolved, I hope, by tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, is there any witness you would -- could call at this moment. MR. DI FAZIO: There is not, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Then if there's no other procedural matter left to discuss at this moment and if there's no other evidence to be heard, the Chamber has no choice but to adjourn until tomorrow, quarter past 2.00, same courtroom.
